## Original definition (verbatim)

1. **FOS-000001 — Preserve precise context in existing diagnostics.** **S; no dependencies; §5.** Pipeline creation failure logs discard the available `VkResult` at [replay:1559](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1559), with analogous compute/ray-tracing branches. Device setup similarly reduces failures to prose. Include phase, resource type/hash and raw numeric result; capture `errno`/`GetLastError()` immediately at OS failures. Fix compute/ray-tracing capture messages incorrectly naming graphics/compute in [dispatch:918](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/layer/dispatch.cpp#L918) and nearby ray-tracing paths. Start with these sites, then extend per subsystem. **Check:** inject distinct Vulkan results and verify distinguishable evidence. Do not classify every non-success as a driver crash or every capture rejection as unsupported pNext. This delivers immediate value before a common schema exists.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Unit tests with Vulkan/OS failure injection:** Distinct injected Vulkan results and OS errors retain their exact numeric values, phase and known resource identity after cleanup; an intervening OS call cannot overwrite the originating error.
   - **Captured-diagnostic assertions:** Compute and ray-tracing failures name the correct resource type. Controlled Vulkan errors and capture rejections do not claim a driver crash or unsupported feature without evidence; a successful control case emits no failure diagnostic.

4. **FOS-000004 — Retain unrecoverable child loss in the controller.** **S–M; no dependencies; §2–§4.** [Linux shutdown:335](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L335) and [Windows shutdown:278](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L278) use the same boolean for “do not restart because done” and “cannot continue.” Their callers restart conditionally but otherwise continue to exit success ([Linux:1429](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1429), [Windows:1035](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L1035)). Separate restart disposition from the retained worker outcome. Immediately return an aggregate unsuccessful result when assigned required work is unresolved. **Check:** E5/E6; clean worker; failed worker alongside a clean worker; failure before resource identity is known. Record the assigned range and unknown remainder. Do not fail all successfully recovered attempts just because a child once died.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Controller subprocess tests on Linux and Windows:** A worker lost before its first progress report produces an unsuccessful controller outcome, retaining its assigned range and unknown remainder. Repeat with another worker succeeding and with worker report order reversed; the unsuccessful aggregate is unchanged.
   - **Recovery control tests:** Clean completion succeeds; a failed attempt followed by verified completion of every required item can succeed. A skipped required culprit or unresolved range cannot succeed. Assert the controller result directly, independently of stderr and optional shared progress.

5. **FOS-000005 — Separate replay-thread work completion from item success.** **M; depends on `FOS-000001` and `FOS-000004` for complete propagation; §2–§3.** [worker:1800](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1800) discards the parse return and increments `completed_count` after processing; creation helpers return void. [normal replay:4553](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L4553) returns success after the queue finishes (E7). Introduce a thread-safe outcome accumulator independent of optional shared memory. First cover parse/read and Vulkan creation failures, then setup/validation/support/dependency exits. Propagate the result through normal replay, child and controller. **Check:** E7, missing entry, injected Vulkan failure, and mixed success/failure. Keep queue progress as queue progress. Unsupported required work must be unsuccessful under the declared policy, even when it is not a crash.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Replay unit and CLI integration tests:** E7, missing input entries, injected creation errors, unsupported required work, validation failures and dependency-blocked work produce the expected distinct outcomes and nonzero aggregate exits. A fully successful workload returns zero.
   - **Thread/mode matrix:** The same fixed mixed workload has the same final logical outcome in normal, child/controller and progress modes, with shared progress absent/present and one/multiple threads. Queue completion still reaches its expected count even when processing fails; it is never the success oracle.

7. **FOS-000007 — Record timeout origin before invoking crash recovery.** **S–M; depends on `FOS-000004`; §4–§5.** [no-progress wait:965](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L965) invokes the timeout handler before its diagnostic. [Linux:1589](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1589) sends SIGABRT; [Windows:1203](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L1203) writes `CRASH`. Store/send a distinct trigger from the healthy dispatcher before termination. Distinguish configured work-no-progress timeout, controller heartbeat timeout, and post-crash cleanup timeout. Include actual monotonic elapsed time and configured threshold. **Check:** deterministic no-progress injection, spontaneous fault, heartbeat loss, failed signal delivery and escalation. An externally observed SIGKILL alone does not prove a controller timeout or OOM. Multiple threads imply unknown individual attribution unless independently established.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Fake-clock and termination-adapter unit tests:** Each configured no-progress, heartbeat and cleanup deadline records its own trigger, threshold and monotonic elapsed time before requesting termination. Progress resets only the applicable deadline; a spontaneous fault has no invented timeout trigger.
   - **Controller integration tests:** Injected SIGABRT/Windows recovery, failed termination delivery and escalation preserve trigger, mechanism and final effect separately. An unexplained external SIGKILL remains unattributed; multi-thread cases without item evidence retain unknown attribution. Use synchronization barriers, not timing races, to order events.

Start with the envelope, reporting invalid shape versus incompatible version; audit nested field reads in subsequent bounded patches. Preserve numeric parse error/offset and resource identity without dumping shader contents. **Check:** `{}`, `[]`, null, missing/string version, malformed nested records; none may assert, terminate the embedding host or be blamed on the driver. Test release and debug builds. This is an outcome/containment prerequisite, not merely prettier logging; no claim of a complete parser-security audit is made here.

   - **Containment and input-mutation tests:** A subprocess sentinel continues after each rejected input; valid fixtures still parse identically. A fixed-seed mutation corpus is run automatically with a bounded runtime, and newly found failures become deterministic fixtures. Diagnostics expose available error offsets/identity but no shader payload.

assertions: Register replay-support-compute with explicit Release-active checks. Synthetic non-null feature initialization; a supported control returns true and clears a reused result.

Exercise actual descriptorBuffer/subgroup feature rejection, a real extension-bearing pNext rejection, maxComputeWorkGroupSize or maxComputeWorkGroupInvocations rejection using registered module entry-point information, and unknown pNext sType. Assert exact support kind, stable feature/extension/property identifier, known observed/required values and raw unknown sType. Reject before driver creation.
Keep previous bool compute_pipeline_is_supported caller results identical; distinguish missing/invalid module metadata from a known feature limit rather than inventing device support facts.

Register replay-support-graphics. Supported graphics control and independently selected real feature (for example depthClamp), extension, existing property-limit (for example multiview/mesh output/subgroup limits), and unknown nested pNext rejection.

Assert exact originating identifier and observed/required fields where the detector has values; nested predicate failure must preserve the specific reason rather than overwrite it with a generic graphics rejection. Unrelated disabled features must not steal attribution.

Register replay-support-raytracing. Supported control; rayTracingPipeline feature, VK_KHR_pipeline_library extension, maxRayRecursionDepth and maxRayHitAttributeSize boundaries, and unknown stage/group/library pNext cases.
Assert correct identifier, required input versus available property values, known bits, and identical old bool support decisions. Boundary equality succeeds and one-over-limit rejects.

Register replay-support-static. Cover sampler, descriptor-set layout, pipeline layout, shader module, render pass and render pass2 entrypoints with supported controls and applicable feature/extension/unknown-sType rejections.

Static-family property tests exercise actual maxPushConstantsSize/maxBoundDescriptorSets and available render-pass limits; sampler has no independent property-limit predicate and must not gain fabricated policy just to fill a test matrix. Document precise applicability in the fixture table.

Check exact SPIR-V capability/extension identifiers and unknown capability values for shader support rejection; malformed SPIR-V and creation OOM remain distinguishable from unsupported. Feature/extension/property/unknown-sType coverage spans every migrated family and each static entrypoint has actual supported/rejected coverage.

Register replay-support-categories using actual parser/filter/Vulkan producer paths: invalid JSON/module parse, SPIR-V validation rejection, VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY, VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY, known support rejection and missing dependency.

Assert returned outcome/category, exact signed Vulkan result where available, zero unsupported counts for parse/OOM/dependency failures, zero creation counts for unsupported/blocked work, and a valid succeeding control after every failure. Do not promise allocator-exhaustion containment beyond controlled existing producers.

Register replay-dependency-module-fanout. A dependency-complete recorded/checked FOZ graph has one invalid or controlled-failed shader module referenced by N distinct pipelines, with N at least 4, across compute/graphics/raytracing consumers as applicable.

Drive actual production parse/resolve/enqueue/creation paths rather than manually setting dependency_blocked. Assert exactly one originating module failure per worker attempt, N distinct blocked consumer identities, every edge names the actual parent tag/hash and its known failure category, and zero Vulkan pipeline creation calls for blocked consumers.

Cover invalid module and a controlled shader-creation failure separately; positive graph creates every expected pipeline. Repeat with one and multiple workers within the ThreadedReplayer process and more than one pipeline memory context. No global cross-process logical-item reconciliation claim is introduced.

Register replay-dependency-parent-fanout. One real failed derivative base or pipeline library has N consumers; exercise compute/graphics derivative paths and graphics/raytracing library paths supported by production infrastructure.

Assert one originating parent creation failure, N linked blocked consumers and zero creation calls for those consumers. Include missing and nested library identities; original hash/tag must survive native handle resolution and sorted dependency scheduling.

A valid parent/consumer control succeeds. Multiple missing parents may retain one bounded first blocker with explicit omitted detail; never fabricate an arbitrary parent or count unattempted consumers as compiler faults.

Register replay-dependency-common-cache. Generate/check actual outer FOZ inputs with a consumer reference omitted from the common-cache/input dependency set: shader, layout/static dependency and base/library parent variants where represented.

Assert missing dependency reason plus exact consumer and missing parent tag/hash, no driver-failure raw result or compiler-fault attribution, zero consumer creation calls, unsuccessful aggregate outcome, and successful equivalent graph with common-cache entries restored.

Input read failure, absent resource and malformed present parent remain distinguishable facts; absence is not called device unsupported. Preserve the original parent failure when recursive parse is involved.

Register replay-dependency-static. Drive sampler/descriptor-layout/pipeline-layout/render-pass dependency substitution paths with real recorded hashes. A failed or missing static parent names the correct edge rather than becoming a new generic consumer Parse/Create failure.

Retain source identities before remapping handles, including static resolve through maintenance4 PipelineResolver. Known originating vkCreate failure stays attached to the static parent; blocked pipeline has no creation call. Successful lazy and ordinary static resolution controls retain expected handles and cleanup.

Register replay-support-call-scope. Per-call detail receivers have value lifetime independent of create-info/pNext storage. Reuse clears stale values; nested calls preserve the first specific origin and independent reentrant calls keep separate receivers.

Barrier-controlled concurrent checks on the same initialized FeatureFilter produce their own exact reasons with no cross-thread leakage. If a callback sink is chosen, explicitly test its documented threading, lifetime/reentrancy and bounded error behavior; a value-output-only design avoids a new callback boundary.
Dependency capture context cannot outlive the parser callback or allocator/memory context; retain only scalar/value identities in queued work and worker frames.

Register replay-support-worker-details and replay-dependency-worker-details using actual detector-to-production-worker/controller pipe paths, extending existing #18 fixtures rather than hand-constructed controller summaries.

With prose disabled, assert support identifier/kind/known values and dependency consumer/parent tag/hash/category, exact worker/attempt, unsuccessful native/final outcome, and positive completion control. Human diagnostics present the same observed facts; no guessed upgrade/extension advice.

Explicitly document/version private detail transport. Preserve existing parse/create/timeout event semantics, HELLO/FINAL uncertainty, legacy lines and absent negotiation; unknown or malformed new details cannot certify supported/successful work.

implementation: Add structured support detail with stable kind/reason identifiers, feature/extension/property names, raw unknown sType/capability and explicit known required/available values. Recursive parse preserves originating parent reason; queued work owns scalar consumer/parent identities. Missing static/common-cache references become blocked dependency facts rather than fresh consumer compiler/parse faults.

Unify blocked consumer recording across shader resolution, static/lazy maintenance4 resolver, derivative base and pipeline-library ordering. Record one originating failure for one cached failed dependency within a worker attempt and one blocked observation per affected logical consumer. Preserve parent failure category when known; mark missing/unknown distinctly. Never call the consumer Vulkan create branch when blocked.

Extend bounded private worker support/dependency detail and controller retention using the existing #18 architecture, documenting exact version/unknown-field rules and count scope. Human messages derive from the same facts. Keep aggregate category counts independent from bounded examples/omission and retain legacy protocol, native termination and FINAL semantics. 1. **FOS-000001 — Preserve precise context in existing diagnostics.** **S; no dependencies; §5.** Pipeline creation failure logs discard the available `VkResult` at [replay:1559](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1559), with analogous compute/ray-tracing branches. Device setup similarly reduces failures to prose. Include phase, resource type/hash and raw numeric result; capture `errno`/`GetLastError()` immediately at OS failures. Fix compute/ray-tracing capture messages incorrectly naming graphics/compute in [dispatch:918](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/layer/dispatch.cpp#L918) and nearby ray-tracing paths. Start with these sites, then extend per subsystem. **Check:** inject distinct Vulkan results and verify distinguishable evidence. Do not classify every non-success as a driver crash or every capture rejection as unsupported pNext. This delivers immediate value before a common schema exists.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Unit tests with Vulkan/OS failure injection:** Distinct injected Vulkan results and OS errors retain their exact numeric values, phase and known resource identity after cleanup; an intervening OS call cannot overwrite the originating error.
   - **Captured-diagnostic assertions:** Compute and ray-tracing failures name the correct resource type. Controlled Vulkan errors and capture rejections do not claim a driver crash or unsupported feature without evidence; a successful control case emits no failure diagnostic.

## Original definition (verbatim)

4. **FOS-000004 — Retain unrecoverable child loss in the controller.** **S–M; no dependencies; §2–§4.** [Linux shutdown:335](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L335) and [Windows shutdown:278](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L278) use the same boolean for “do not restart because done” and “cannot continue.” Their callers restart conditionally but otherwise continue to exit success ([Linux:1429](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1429), [Windows:1035](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L1035)). Separate restart disposition from the retained worker outcome. Immediately return an aggregate unsuccessful result when assigned required work is unresolved. **Check:** E5/E6; clean worker; failed worker alongside a clean worker; failure before resource identity is known. Record the assigned range and unknown remainder. Do not fail all successfully recovered attempts just because a child once died.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Controller subprocess tests on Linux and Windows:** A worker lost before its first progress report produces an unsuccessful controller outcome, retaining its assigned range and unknown remainder. Repeat with another worker succeeding and with worker report order reversed; the unsuccessful aggregate is unchanged.
   - **Recovery control tests:** Clean completion succeeds; a failed attempt followed by verified completion of every required item can succeed. A skipped required culprit or unresolved range cannot succeed. Assert the controller result directly, independently of stderr and optional shared progress.

## Original definition (verbatim)

5. **FOS-000005 — Separate replay-thread work completion from item success.** **M; depends on `FOS-000001` and `FOS-000004` for complete propagation; §2–§3.** [worker:1800](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1800) discards the parse return and increments `completed_count` after processing; creation helpers return void. [normal replay:4553](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L4553) returns success after the queue finishes (E7). Introduce a thread-safe outcome accumulator independent of optional shared memory. First cover parse/read and Vulkan creation failures, then setup/validation/support/dependency exits. Propagate the result through normal replay, child and controller. **Check:** E7, missing entry, injected Vulkan failure, and mixed success/failure. Keep queue progress as queue progress. Unsupported required work must be unsuccessful under the declared policy, even when it is not a crash.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Replay unit and CLI integration tests:** E7, missing input entries, injected creation errors, unsupported required work, validation failures and dependency-blocked work produce the expected distinct outcomes and nonzero aggregate exits. A fully successful workload returns zero.
   - **Thread/mode matrix:** The same fixed mixed workload has the same final logical outcome in normal, child/controller and progress modes, with shared progress absent/present and one/multiple threads. Queue completion still reaches its expected count even when processing fails; it is never the success oracle.

## Original definition (verbatim)

7. **FOS-000007 — Record timeout origin before invoking crash recovery.** **S–M; depends on `FOS-000004`; §4–§5.** [no-progress wait:965](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L965) invokes the timeout handler before its diagnostic. [Linux:1589](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1589) sends SIGABRT; [Windows:1203](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L1203) writes `CRASH`. Store/send a distinct trigger from the healthy dispatcher before termination. Distinguish configured work-no-progress timeout, controller heartbeat timeout, and post-crash cleanup timeout. Include actual monotonic elapsed time and configured threshold. **Check:** deterministic no-progress injection, spontaneous fault, heartbeat loss, failed signal delivery and escalation. An externally observed SIGKILL alone does not prove a controller timeout or OOM. Multiple threads imply unknown individual attribution unless independently established.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Fake-clock and termination-adapter unit tests:** Each configured no-progress, heartbeat and cleanup deadline records its own trigger, threshold and monotonic elapsed time before requesting termination. Progress resets only the applicable deadline; a spontaneous fault has no invented timeout trigger.
   - **Controller integration tests:** Injected SIGABRT/Windows recovery, failed termination delivery and escalation preserve trigger, mechanism and final effect separately. An unexplained external SIGKILL remains unattributed; multi-thread cases without item evidence retain unknown attribution. Use synchronization barriers, not timing races, to order events.

Preserve numeric parse error/offset and resource identity without dumping shader contents. **Check:** `{}`, `[]`, null, missing/string version, malformed nested records; none may assert, terminate the embedding host or be blamed on the driver.    - **Containment and input-mutation tests:** A subprocess sentinel continues after each rejected input; valid fixtures still parse identically. A fixed-seed mutation corpus is run automatically with a bounded runtime, and newly found failures become deterministic fixtures. Diagnostics expose available error offsets/identity but no shader payload.
